newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bids to allow doctors to withhold care.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bids to allow doctors to withhold care.

text.p: A Canadian legislator said on Tuesday she had introduced legislation to protect doctors from prosecution if they withhold or withdraw life-sustaining treatment from patients who request this.

Debate began on Tuesday on the Senate bill, which would also allow doctors to administer pain control medication "with the intention of alleviating the physical pain of the patient, in dosages which may shorten life," a statement said.

Most bills that pass both houses of Parliament start in the elected House of Commons, but occasionally proceedings of the unelected Senate wins the support of the government, especially on tricky social issues.
Liberal Sen. Sharon Carstairs introduced the bill last week to try to implement two of the recommendations from a special Senate committee on euthanasia and assisted suicide.
The committee was split on the most contentious issues but she said it was unanimous on pain control and withholding and withdrawing treatment.

"Although the committee recognized that the withholding and withdrawal of life-sustaining treatment is legal, it heard evidence as to the reluctance on the part of some medical practitioners to honor the wishes of patients for fear of being held liable," Carstairs stated.
Similarly doctors often are reluctant to provide enough pain control medication for fear of being held liable, she added.

"The great tragedy is that patients are not always receiving adequate palliative care and therefore patients suffering from extreme physical pain find that their only alternative is to ask for assisted suicide and euthanasia to end their suffering," she said.
If it passes the Senate, it will proceed to the House.
